name: BrickHouse Scene

evidence.observation: The right facade is visible from its front corner to the rearward boundary; combined with the front-width anchor and the three-level facade height, it bounds a depth modestly smaller than the 10 m front width.
The wide left-side view independently shows the main side-wall run and rear/deck zone, supporting the same approximate depth range.
The rear-left oblique view closes the rearward extent of the main mass and rules out a substantially deeper envelope.
The nearly frontal facade provides a pixel height-to-known-width ratio from ground line to the wall/roof junction across three visible opening levels.
The right-side view independently constrains the wall height relative to the same three-level envelope.
The closer left-side view confirms the upper opening level and wall-to-roof junction relative to the lower exterior structures.
Main target envelope and three stacked opening levels are visible.
The same envelope is visible along the right side.
The same envelope is visible along the left side.
The same envelope is visible from the rear-left.
The low rendered volume projects outward from the left side by roughly a quarter of the known front width when compared across the closer left view.
The rear-left view confirms the outward projection and its junction with the stair.
The visible side and bay face bound the low volume as a short rear-side block rather than a long wing.
The rear-left oblique view independently bounds its front-to-rear extent beside the stair.
The top of the low volume sits a little above the large bay and well below the main upper window; comparison to the metrized main envelope bounds its height.
The same top level is visible beside the stair in the rear-left view.
Distinct low rendered exterior volume with a large bay.
Same low volume visible beside the stair from rear-left.
Upper-left front opening metrized proportionally against the 10 m facade width and inferred facade height.
Upper-right front opening metrized proportionally against the 10 m facade width and inferred facade height.
Middle-left front opening metrized from its rectangle and ordering on the nearly frontal facade.
Middle-right front opening metrized from its rectangle and ordering on the nearly frontal facade.
Certain lower-left physical opening; size and position are bounded from the front view, while the Survey only makes the window semantic type plausible.
Tall glazed entrance-sized lower-right opening; rectangle is metrized proportionally from the known facade width and inferred facade height.
Elevated right-side window bounded relative to the metrized side-wall run and main envelope height.
Certain low rectangular opening near the rearward right wall; metric rectangle is bounded, but window semantics remain only plausible in the Survey.
Upper left-side window located using the canonical rear-left-origin facade offset and the wide side view.
Closer left-side view refines its height and position relative to the roof edge and low volume.
Rear-left view confirms the same opening and prevents a mirrored placement.
Certain lower framed opening behind the deck; metric rectangle is approximate and no semantic type is asserted by the Survey.
Large dark bay occupies most of the low volume facade; size is bounded against that multi-view volume.
Rear-left view confirms the same physical bay and its vertical extent.
The roof edge visibly falls from the front toward the rear on the right facade, supporting a mono-pitch/shed hypothesis.
A shallow roof is visibly present above the front facade, but the frontal perspective does not by itself establish a numeric rise/run.
The roof edge continues above the left facade.
The rear-left view confirms roof continuity but does not provide a sufficiently calibrated rise/run for a defensible numeric pitch.

The long right-side roof edge shows a substantial continuous fall from front toward rear, ruling out an almost-flat roof, while perspective foreshortening prevents treating the apparent image angle as the physical pitch.
The closer left-side view independently shows the same mono-pitch fall; its oblique camera angle supports only a broad physical pitch interval rather than one exact angle.
The rear-left view confirms roof continuity and the rear low side; together with the two side views it supports a conservative bounded pitch while not calibrating an exact rise/run.

Street and curb show a longitudinal grade along the right facade. The Survey treats the exact front-to-rear direction as only plausible, so the Scene asserts neither metric endpoint elevation nor numeric amplitude.
Raised timber deck and balustrade are visible along the left/rear portion of the building; its extent is bounded relative to the side facade.
The deck begins immediately beside the low exterior volume and visibly meets the main wall.
Visible exterior stair rises beside the low volume with solid rendered parapets.
Rear-left view shows the same flight from ground to the junction with the low volume, constraining its run and top level.

evidence.observation: Bay boundaries are formed by the low white volume.

evidence.observation: Deck edge meets the white building facade.
Same deck meets the target building in the second left-side view.

relations.statement: The stair is visibly contiguous with the low exterior volume.

evidence.observation: Stair/parapet physically meets the low white volume.
The same stair-volume junction is visible again.

relations.statement: The low exterior volume visibly abuts the target building.

evidence.observation: Low white volume directly meets the main building wall.
Same junction recurs in rear-left view.

relations.statement: The timber deck visibly meets the low exterior volume at their common edge.

evidence.observation: Deck begins immediately at the side of the low white volume with a visible common boundary.

notes: Metric preflight used all five photo views. volume_main.depth and height are low/moderate-confidence inferred bounds from the 10 m front-width anchor and multi-view facade proportions; lower_exterior_volume, timber_deck and exterior_stair are jointly metrized so every Survey connects_to relation whose contact is visibly established is geometrically resolved. roof_main existence is certain in the Survey, while roof_type='shed' is only plausible; the Scene therefore preserves type='shed' as an inference and leaves pitch_degrees null because the side-view pixels do not provide a sufficiently calibrated rise/run. ArchitecturalScene v0.2 has no shed slope-direction field, so no direction is invented. The right-side terrain grade certainly exists, but its direction is only plausible and its amplitude is unmeasured; both grade endpoint elevations therefore remain null. Survey context objects neighbor_left and neighbor_right are not rendered because v0.2 has no context primitive; their adjacency remains authoritative in the Survey rather than being converted into invented Scene geometry. Part-of relations to the semantic building boundary are represented by Scene volume_id/roof volume_id ownership; lower_volume_opening_part_of_volume is serialized explicitly because both Scene endpoints exist. Physical connects_to relations whose contact is visible are preserved explicitly and resolved. roof_main down_slope_direction is preserved as rear from multi-view evidence. The five reference photos support only a conservative 10–35 degree pitch interval: the side views rule out an almost-flat roof, while oblique perspective prevents a defensible exact angle. pitch_degrees therefore remains null and no midpoint, endpoint, or default angle is selected.
